input.prompt: Follow the second reference image's layout exactly. A single vintage 1970s ceramic EPROM chip in a long, deep dual in-line package, seen perfectly straight on from the front, perfectly horizontal, flat, symmetric, centred, filling the width; the body's height is about a third of its length. The ceramic body is a LIGHT NEUTRAL PALE GREY enamel, no colour cast at all, evenly lit, with a fine matte grain and a thin gold seal ring. LEFT END: one flat empty square gold plate, blank, in the upper half only; below it a smooth bare flat stretch of the same pale grey ceramic, blank. Between the gold plate and the label: one PERFECTLY SQUARE quartz glass window (its width exactly equal to its height, not a tall rectangle), slightly rounded corners, set flush in a thin gold frame, as tall as the label panel and therefore as wide as it is tall, through it a dark empty black cavity, completely blank. RIGHT HALF: one large flat empty rectangular label panel of matte black epoxy with a very fine grain and a thin gold border, blank, taking the whole right half of the body and nearly its full height. Evenly spaced gold legs along the top and bottom edges. Painted light: soft even light from the front, a thin green rim light on the left edge and a thin red rim light on the right edge, the void around it dark. Painted comic book illustration in exactly the style of the first reference image (the green NVIDIA chip): a real object drawn sharp with clean black ink outlines on every part, comic halftone dots only inside the shadows. The object alone on a pure black void. Absolutely no text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no symbols, no flags, no signs, no markings anywhere.
